title: Dylan’s Crazy Ex Girlfriend
post: Slacked an easy 10 miles or so from Dalton to Cheshire with Dylan. We were planning to go to Greylock today, but won’t make it there until tomorrow. When we stopped in town for lunch and a beer Dylan’s ex-girlfriend showed up at the bar! She had driven all the way from Boston and was searching for us all day. It was a ton of drama, a big change from the camp-hike-camp-hike of the last several days. Dyland and I ran away and hid behind St. Mary’s Church in Cheshire, where he slept in the car and I setup my tent. They let hikers stay there for free so long as you clean up after yourself. It’s nice to be close to towns and have so many options for nice places to stay the last few nights.

title: Dalton
post: Stayed in Dalton with Puddles. There is a nice old guy (with STRICT quiet hours and rules) who lets hikers camp in his backyard, along the trail. I got a really great fish n chips and some local beer at the bar around the corner before bed. In the morning I met Dylan to go slack and hike a bit with him the next day. I invited lots of friends to come hike with me, but everyone is busy with their own lives. I was so excited to see Dylan and have him be part of my adventure.

title: Stratton Mtn & Pond
post: This pin is at Stratton Pond. I met my Dad for the first time in a long while today at a parking lot on the side of the trail at the bottom of Stratton Mountain.  He hiked up the moutain with me and Lids, then slacked us another 18 miles to Manchester Center, VT. At the bottom of the mountain is this huge awesome pond where we stopped to put my hands and legs in just for a minute before continuing to hike.  I got rained on pretty hard for 2 hours today, but it was okay because I knew that I had all my stuff in the nice dry car. Hiking wet isn’t so bad when all my stuff is still dry. Stratton Mountain / Pond is cool because it’s where Benton MacKaye had the idea to start the AT. I definitely know why, it’s so gorgeous. The whole hike today was a great representation for why Vermont is so nice to hike in: big mountains with great views that make it worth it, glacial lakes, cold clear springs, etc.. I love hiking in VT.

title: Green Mountain House
post: Taking a 0 today at the Green Mountain House Hostel.  I stayed here in 2016 near the end of my first big hike. I got a free pint of Ben and Jerry’s when I walked in and my new pair of Oboz shoes were waiting for me. I went to town, got to use a computer for the first time in a while, got new socks to go with my new shoes, resupplied, and relaxed a lot. I really needed a day off. Feeling refreshed and ready to take on the mountains of VT, NH, and ME. Puddles and Fudge left here this morning, so I will probably see them again. I’m feeling really happy and content with where I am on the trail and how it’s going. A lot of people are saying they don’t want it to end and will start going slower, but I just want to finish. Heading out EARLY tomorrow and getting back to the grind. Ready for the last 2.5 states!

title: The End Of Rocks
post: Today I'm taking my first 0 day since leaving West Virginia. Andrew and I are stopped at Delaware Water Gap, staying at the Church of the Mountain, a free hostel. We're .3 mile from crossing the Delaware and entering NJ. I'm so happy to be done PA. Kait and Mike, who I met in the Smokies while they were doing a section, live nearby. They said they would visit me if I called them when I got here. We met at the church around noon and went bowling, to Wal-Mart, and for good NJ pizza. It was great to do some indoor activities for once. Feeling rejuvenated and ready to crush the last 900 miles.

title: A million degrees
post: Today it was at least a million degrees out. It was hot yesterday, but today was killer. I got up at sunrise and hiked from Pochuck Mountain Shelter to NJ 94, only 7 miles. I left without Andrew for the first time since we've been hiking together. I just wanted some alone time. At the road was Mitch's Roadside Hotdog Stand and Heaven Hill Farm, which has icecream and cider donuts. They had a green house with misting sprinklers that I stood in eating icecream for an hour, when Andrew caught up again. Together we hitched to Warwick NY and stayed at the drive in movie theatre, where this pin is. I've never been to one before and they let hikers camp on the hill in the back. The dozens of hikers there watched movies and ate snacks instead of hiking since it was just too hot. Back to the trail in the morning!

title: First day back
post: Today Alex and I left our favorite hotel from hell, The Towns Inn early in the morning. I'm currently writing this in the bathroom at Dahlgren Campground MD. We're completely drenched from rain that started 10 minutes after we got here, while I was setting up my tent, which is now wet inside. Within 3 hours of starting today I had been stung by bees twice and pooped on by a bird. At least I got a dry place to sit and got to take a hot shower at the campground. Is that the universe telling me to stop and not hike any more? Or is it punishing me for taking a week off in DC? The only way to know is to keep hiking tomorrow!

title: Sucked into the vortex
post: There is a term, ‘the vortex’ or ‘getting vortexed’ or ‘vortexing’. That’s what I’m doing today. It’s when a hiker says they aren’t going to stay in town for very long… but then they do.  I’m staying at the Angels Rest Hiker Heaven Hostel in Pearisburg VA for 2 days. It’s so nice here. I am cooking in a full kitchen for the first time since I got out here. I love to cook, and didn’t realise that it’s one of the things I miss the most while I’m out here.

title: The Barn & Quarter Way
post: Stopped at a restaurant on the side of the highway in Atkins called The Barn with Catalog. It was cheap and had the best potato salad I’ve ever had EVER. But I stayed inside The Barn for like 3 hours since it was raining hard and ended up doing a short day, finishing at the Quarter Way Hostel., mile 555\. I was so wet I just couldn’t take being outside tonight. The hostel was nice and Sartec was there too, he was the guy that got us set up with kayaks at Boots Off. We played board games until bed and ate ice cream.

title: Lindamood School House
post: Staying the night with Catalog in the Lindamood School House. It’s a little shack on the side of the trail that was a school house a 150 years and a local Baptist Church fills some tubs in a wooden box with snacks, soda, and health care products for hikers. What great trail magic! The walls of the school house have rules for teachers and rules for students, including how many lashes a student gets. For example, 6 lashes for any boy who goes near girls when they are playing, and 1 lash per foot over 4 feet that a child climbs up a tree. I don’t know how many lashes I would get for sleeping inside the school house museum… so we will get up early and not get in trouble. Hikers all write nice things and their names on the chalk boards, it was a super cool place to stay over.

title: Marion
post: Made it to Marion from Dickey Gap in time for breakfast at McDonalds. I ate 4 breakfast sandwiches, a burger, and a large fries…. And a chocolate shake… and some kombucha at Walgreens.  Resupplied at Walmart and met Catalog there, so we had Chinese for lunch together. Catalog is a very photogenic hiker from Switzerland and we talked about the differences between hiking here in America and the trails he has done in the Alps in Europe. There’s a shuttle around Marion that is $0.50, which also goes to the Pat Jennings Visitor Center, which is a small state park right along the AT. So Catalog and I went back to the trail in the early afternoon to keep hiking.

title: Grayson Highlands
post: Went through Grayson, took lots of pictures today. Got bit by a baby wild pony near this pin. It was funny, and a great day of hiking over the rolling hills to a Baptist Church in Troutdale which runs a donation based hostel, just a few miles off the trail. Got a nice shower and made sure the pony didn’t actually break my skin. I will definitely come back to this area to see the wild ponies again.

title: And I would walk 500 miles...
post:
Thomas Knob Shelter, just before Grayson Highlands, Elk Park was cool too. I met Quartz in the shelter, he was very nice but a little insane and told me about how all the ancient pyramids were connected by underground water tubes with electrolytes in them, and they shoot electricity out of the top to use Earth as a giant battery for aliens. Okay buddy. Also met some hipsters doing a Super Cleanse, where they only eat honey, cayenne pepper, lemon juice, and water. Sounds horrible. Today I passed 500 miles of hiking.

AND I WOULD WALK 500 MILES, AND I WOULD WALK 500 MORE, AND I WOULD WALK 500 MORE, AND I WOULD WALK 500 MORE, AND I WOULD WALK 200 MORE.

Tomorrow I’m going through Grayson Highlands, I’m very excited.

title: Damascus
post: Got into Damascus in the late morning with Turbo and Lighthouse. Whiskey and Turkey were taking their time, but I wanted to get to Woodchuck Hostel so I could shower and get the burning evil nettles off my leg. I got to the hostel and they said they weren’t letting hikers in for just showers any more… even though every other hostel on the entire trail does $5 showers for hikers. The owner was very rude to me, even when I explained the situation. I won’t be back. Luckily I have made some nice friends and there are so many amazing people here. Turbo and Lighthouse brought me to the Hiker Inn that they had a room reserved in. The Inn owner used to study bees and agreed to let me have a shower in their very nice Inn if I sit and talk about ants and bees with her afterwards. Good deal!! Rubbed myself with anti-bacterial body wash and calamine lotion, and I’m feeling good again. So good that I’m blowing through Damascus and going to the next shelter, a 28 mile day, my longest yet. Yeehaw and Mousetrap were in town too, along with a huge bubble of like 75 hikers. I got some food at the dollar store, some lunch at the dinner, a new pair of shoes, and I set off along the Creeper Trail (a 50 mile bike trail which is parallel with the AT for several miles after Damascus). Maybe one day I’ll come back for some bike riding here.

title: evil stinging nettles
post: At Double Springs Shelter with Whiskey, Turkey, Turbo, and Lighthouse. I was getting my food bag down from the tree and tripped on a log. The log scraped my right shin pretty bad, and I fell into a patch of stinging nettles. My whole left leg was swollen, and burning, the skin was bubbling, and I was having a bad time.

title: Aqua Blaze
post: Turbo, Lighthouse, Turkey, Whiskey, and I went aqua blazing. That means you skip part of the trail and go over water. Boots Off Hostel let you rent kayaks for the day. Instead of hiking about 18 miles around Watauga Lake, or…. We can kayak about 10 miles through the lake, have a nice lunch on an island with a rope swing, swim a little, and then get a ride at the other end of the lake to the trail head. We chose the latter.

title: Golden Retriever Hiker Home
post:
Porridge gave me the number for a Hiker Home in Hampton. You have to say who gave you the number and be invited to go. I stayed there tonight, it was so nice and included a nice southern home cooked meal of grilled chicken legs, rice & beans, biscuits, water melon; a huge breakfast of 5 eggs, toast, bacon; and I got to play with all their golden retrievers (the best part!).

Whiskey and Turkey stayed at Boots Off Hostel, I’ll catch up with them again tomorrow.

title: Laurel Falls
post: Biggest waterfall I’ve seen. Just passed mile 420, and there was a guy there with 2 cute dogs giving thru hikers cupcakes.

title: Super 0
post: Taking a Zero Day in Johnson City with Whiskey and Turkey. Whiskey had a friend in the area so Turkey and I went to see the new Pokemon movie and played video games and ate fast food. The hotel had a pool I used a lot, and a ‘office center’ which was a computer from 2012 that crashed when I opened chrome. Great zero day.

title: Big Red Barn
post: Stayed at Overmountain Shelter, a huge big red barn, converted into an AT shelter that can sleep 40\. Ivy (the friendly black lab) and Porridge showed up just after I did, I haven't seen them since Franklin. Ivy totally remembered me and snuggled me in the night. I had a big fight with an old guy doing an overnight because he was starting a fire in the middle of the grass, not in a fire circle, which is very dangerous. Porridge backed me up. Beautiful views from the shelter, and I got a bunch of cool 360 pictures here. Turkey and Whiskey are here too. This is my favorite shelter so far.

title: Mountain Harbor & Burgers
post: Did my miles and was planning to go to Mountain Harbor hostel for ‘the best breakfast on the trail’. They run a big B&B and also have a hostel for hikers. The B&B seemed really nice but when I got there I was told the ‘stinky hikers go to shack basement over there!’ I thought they were a bit rude so I ordered a half pound burger and onion rings. I ordered another big burger before I left and packed it out for dinner at Mountaineer Shelter. My friend Yeehaw (who i haven't seen since Fontana) was there, and Mouse Trap, No Rain, Whiskey, and Turkey, plus several other hikers. Everyone was jealous of the burger I packet out, it was awesome.

title: Slack to Greasy Creek & CHICKEN POT PIE
post: Turkey, Whiskey, and I paid $30 to the shuttle driver at the hostel in Erwin to have our packs shuttled to The Greasy Creek Friendly, about 25 miles North. We wanted to put some distance between us and some unfriendly folks at Uncle Johnny’s. Greasy Creek Friendly is a hostel in the middle of the woods run by some very conservative jewish folks who had chicken pot pies. I bought (and ate) 4 chicken pot pies while I was there, and some soda and ice cream. The place was hard to find and Whiskey didn’t make it until just after dark. They folks running the hostel told us their neighbors keep knocking down rock piles and signs that they put up, directly people 0.5 miles down a side trail from the AT to the hostel. On our way out in the morning we put up some rocks to help other hikers find it. This is a great niche place I would come back to and eat more chicken pot pie.

title: No Chinese Food
post: It’s Memorial Day and the Chinese food place in Erwin is closed. All is lost. There is no hope. The world is dying. Whiskey, Turkey, and I are sad.

title: Uncle Johnny’s
post: Hiked an easy 6.5 miles down from the shelter to Erwin, TN for my next resupply and Chinese food. There is a hostel called Uncle Johnny’s with 100 bunks for hikers that is right on the side of the river and 25 feet from the AT. I planned to stay with Turkey and Whiskey there, but there was a bit of rabble and some sketchy characters that we didn’t want to sleep near. So the three of us went into Erwin and shared a cheap hotel room at Super 8\. We got a ride in the back of a truck from a local to the grocery store across town, it was not safe but hey, gotta get there somehow. The town seemed kind of shook and not as friendly to hikers as most AT towns, since the murder in VA a few weeks ago. Apparently, the sheriff in Erwin had the murderer in custody a week before it happened, but let him go. People are angry about it, that’s a lot of drama for a town of 400.

title: Big Bald
post: Today I was planning to hike to Big Bald Mountain Shelter. This is really the first huge bald that I’ve gone over, similar to Max Patch more of a mountain. Big Bald is 5516 feet, a big climb that I did with Turkey and Whiskey most of the day. They’re funny guys that are hiking together and are from Florida. Turkey is a nerdy accountant and we talked about crypto currencies most of the day. Then the shelter was not great and it was windy so we kept going to No Business Knob Shelter. I left them in the late afternoon to go faster and they got to the shelter well after dark, since they both took a nap on top of Big Bald. While that sounds nice, it doesn’t make up for how horrible night hiking is.

title: Carvers Gap
post: Carvers Gap, Jane Bald, Round Bald… all incredible. Huge rolling hills, and the first place on the trail where you can see the AT winding up the mountain. Seeing where I've gone and where I'm going is surreal. Is that a metaphor for life? Do I know where I'm going in my life?? Yes! To Maine! I must come back here again some day .About to pass 400 miles too.

title: Slack Packing is Awesome & Friendly Cows
post: Slacked the easiest 20 miles I ever did today. The Inn keeper’s son brought our packs 20 miles up the trail and met us at the road crossing with cold gatorade in the early afternoon. I planned to go to Laurel Hostel, but decided to hike 5 more miles to see a waterfall and stay at Hogback Ridge Shelter. We met Whiskey and Turkey, who Turbo and Lighthouse already knew. They had gotten off the trail for a week in Gatlinburg but were back. This pin is in a huge fenced in field that the trail crosses full of friendly cows!

title: Hemlock Hollow Inn
post: In the morning Turbo and Lighthouse passed me. They were slack packing to Hemlock Hollow so I hiked with them all day and they shared their fancy cheeze puffs from Trader Joes with me. There was a fire tower, which was built last year after the big NC forest fires. Finished the day a bit earlier than planned at Hemlock Hollow, a newly opened hostel selling pints of ben and jerry’s. I ate 2\.  This is the first hostel on my list of ‘Definitely Come Back To’. They have a bunch of cute little cabins and a little creek runs through the area. Tomorrow the owner’s son will slack pack me, Turbo, and Lighthouse 25 miles for the first time! I’m excited, and this place is awesome. The inn keeper put down hay in a pavilion that I camped in for $10. I also got a shower. I would go back to this place for sure. It would be a nice place for a family reunion or a mountain retreat for a few days.

title: Hot Springs Day 2
post: Today Alex left me for real. I’m sad without him, but I know I have to hike my own hike. I waited for Alex to get a shuttle to a bigger town where he could get a bus. I left town in the early afternoon. The AT joins a trail called the Lovers Leap Trail right outside of town. There is a legend that a native American woman fell in love with a colonial English man when the area was being settled and conquered by Europeans. But neither side would let the lovers be together, so they leapt from the rocks on top of the mountain outside of Hot Springs.  While I’m sad that Alex has left me, I don’t think I will jump off the mountain. I was planning on doing about 15 miles but the trail goes along the river and it was hot. I ended up taking a long soak in the river and camping right along it in the most beautiful spot ever, with Sunshine and Trillion. Sunshine didn’t hang his food bag, left peanut butter on the ground, and a bear came into our campsite in the middle of the night. I won’t camp with him ever again.

title: Pecks Corner & Horses
post: Staying at Pecks Corner Shelter tonight. I met Ms Christina and her husband, who have 3 horses and a mule with them. They’ve been clearing brush and cutting fallen trees all day and are camping out with us. Ms Christina went down the hill to get water from a spring for the animals. All of the shelters have water sources somewhat nearby, some closer than others. This particular one was down a steep hill about 50 yards. When she came back up the hill she slipped on some mud and spilled her water. Sometimes, after a long day, it doesn’t take much. I thought she was going to cry, since the hill was so steep. So I offered to get water for the horses and made a few trips up and down the hill with the buckets.  Then I got to help feed the horses and become their friend. It was a super fun evening talking with Ms Christina about her horses and petting them. I took a few pictures and gave the big load horse, Milly, lots of scratches behind the ears for doing such good work keeping the trail clean for me and the other hikers.

title: Clingman’s Dome
post: Clingman’s Dome is right at Mile 200, at 6658 feet. It happens to be the highest point on the AT. It’s all downhill from here!! Alex is feeling physically destroyed. We’re going to slow down for the next few days. And the rangers at Clingman’s Dome told us there were several shelter closures coming up because there is a 400 lb bear entering shelters and who has figured  out how to pull on the bear wires that the rangers put up near the shelters, where people hang their food at night. Planning around these closures is hard and slowing us down. The Smokies have been really hard so far and this makes it harder.

title: Shuckstack Fire Tower
post: Just entered the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, the most visited national park in America, with more than 11 Million yearly visitors. We put the bottom half of our Thru Hiker registrations into a metal box at the start of the park. We have to hold the top half of the pass for the rest of the park and put it in another box when we leave the park. Today has been a huge climb moving towards Russell Field Shelter, which is up on the ridge line of the Smokies. This marker is on a fire tower which looks out on the whole Fontana valley. It was the highest fire tower I’ve been on by far. I imagined being the person who lives on the mountain in a hut and hangs out in the fire tower all day just looking for fires, for months at a time.

title: Fontana Day 4
post: I’ve been in Fontana for the 4th day and I need to leave. I had to wait for Alex an extra day so I ended up taking two 0’s. This marker is right on the actual Fontana Dam, which Alex and I walked across on the 14th after he arrived late the night before. The AT goes right across the top of the Dam and you can see the huge stream of water going into the turbines. The top of the dam is flat but the next 8 miles are straight up to get to the ridge line for the Smoky Mountains.

title: Standing Bear
post: Stopped at Standing Bear Farm & Hostel. It was one of the most disgusting places I’ve ever been to. We had planned to stay there or at least get enough food to make it to Hot Springs, but ended up just buying a gatorade and moving on to the next shelter. Yes, I am a dirty smelly hiker, no I don’t want to live in filth or catch a norovirus.

title: Max Patch
post: Max Patch (originally Mack’s Patch, after Mack cleared the top of a mountain for cows a long time ago) is crazy. It’s a huge grassy field at the top of a mountain with views all the way around. It’s larger than an NFL football field, and there were a hundred people hanging around, lounging, playing ball, etc.. It was almost like chilling at the beach… but on a giant flat mountain. There’s a parking lot nearby and most people walk .3 mile from the lot to the Patch. Alex and I hiked about 12 miles to get there in the early afternoon. We met some people that gave us wine and strawberries in exchange for telling them stories about the trail. Then Alex decided he has had enough and got a ride into town, quitting on me. I’ll do the next 25 miles into Hot Springs myself and meet him there tomorrow. Max Patch is definitely somewhere I want to return to, it’s super cool.

title: Hot Springs, NC
post: Just made it to Hot Springs, NC. The Smoky Mountains were very very challenging. I’ve really been pushing my physical limits over the last week. When I got into Hot Springs a few hours ago I ate a 20oz burger at the diner in town. They didn’t think I could eat it all. It was easy since I had already hiked 15 miles to get into town. After eating the whole thing I won a scoop of ice cream and a strawberry cobbler. It was a great change, after eating instant mashed potatoes for a week. There is a real grocery store in town so I can get some better food today, for the next little section of my hike. I’ll post all the updates from the Smokies by tomorrow.

title: My First Zero
post: Taking my first 0 day, where I go exactly 0 miles. I went to the visitor center for Fontana Dam and talked about renewable energy for like 3 hours with Dam workers. They don’t do tours of the inside since 9/11 though. I went to Fontana Village, which I definitely want to return to. It’s super nice, there’s  disc golf course, and lots to do. Too expensive for me to stay there though, and my resupply before the Smokies cost me an arm and a leg. $2.25 for instant mashed potatoes are you kidding me?! Feeling very relaxed, the lake is lovely. Moss and Yeehaw took 0’s today too, and Big Man and Refugee hung out most of the day and stayed the night. Tomorrow I’ll meet my friend Alex and hit the Smokies. It will be really hard but I’m ready!

title: All Roads Lead to Fontana
post: There’s so much water, that when I’ve hiking over rocky sections I can hear the rush of a spring or river under the ground, but not see the water. It’s a very strange phenomenon. The biggest tree I’ve seen since I started was laying down across the trail and I had to climb around it. Saw a ton of newts and salamanders today, they must love how rainy and muddy it is. I am caked in mud. Did I mention it’s wet and muddy today? No matter, I push on with the Fontana Dam ‘Hilton’ shelter on my radar. The shelter has cell reception, and a solar charger for phones that a boy scout troop put in, and showers, or so I’ve heard down the trail. It’s not a real Hilton but compared to most of the shacks in the woods or camping it is. After another 22 mile day I made it just as it was getting dark. The lake looks beautiful. But it was just too rainy and cloudy, the solar charger is not putting out any juice. No charged phone for me, no mother's day for mom, but I did my best. I can get to town tomorrow and call. At least she will know that I was thinking of her and the help she gave me moving out of my apartment so that I could come on this adventure. Meow, Moss, Yeehaw, and the Maine Couple are here, as well as a ton of other friendly hikers I haven’t met yet. Big Man and Refugee are just a couple miles behind and should get in early in tomorrow. We have a nice little trail family coming together. I jumped in the lake and took a shower before bed.

title: The NOC
post:
Today I got rained on so hard. I am wet and cold. I spent most of the day at the NOC, hoping to Bear Jesus that the rain would stop. The pizza was…. decent but very expensive. I paid $20 for a thru hiker pass to stay in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, which I enter after Fontana Dam, and printed it out at the outfitter in NOC. There are lots of rules there. Everyone has to say exactly what shelter they are staying in which day, and you’re only allowed to stay in shelters, no camping in random places. Thru Hikers have some special privileges, like being able to stay in any given shelter, but we have to give up our spots to hikers with reservations. Just a short (extremely wet and cold) hike in the afternoon to the next shelter, which was nearly full. Luckily I got a space. The Maine Couple & Yeehaw were there, who I met at Albert Mountain but he didn’t have a trail name then.

Everyone said there would come a day when I would just have to hike in the pouring rain and just to embrace being wet. I had hoped it wouldn’t be so soon… yet here we are.

title: Made it just in time
post:
Made it as it was getting very dark to the Rufus Morgan Shelter. Just a mile to go in the morning to Nantahala Outdoors Center, which I’ve heard rumors that they have great pizza. Hung my bear bag with the Maine Couple again. We did 22.3 miles today and I am beat! I’m sleeping in the shelter with a hiker named Moss who started a day before me but I havent met yet. Moss is trying to create ‘sense memories’ by touching the moss on the sides of trees while they hike. okay….. Everyone else is tenting tonight because there are TONS of MASSIVE spiders in the shelter. I don’t think they will bother me. We have a common enemy, the evil mosquitos. By the way, I have a million little bug bites and tiny scratches that I don’t know where they came from. Putting neosporin and stuff on them and I feel fine.
Morning Update: I spider attacks and not a single buzzing of a mosquito in my ear. Theres a huge thunder storm coming through so I will wait in the shelter for a bit and take it slow today.

title: The Jump Off, the Spine, the Wesser Bald Fire Tower
post: Today I’m hiking with the Maine Couple. They hike fast and I lost them after lunch time. I’m taking a break at ‘The Jump Off’ at mile 133\. I want to catch up to them before making camp. Today I’ve already gone over an area that was very burned in forest fires 2 years ago. Then i passed the Wesser Bald Fire Tower, which was 4600 feet up and had incredible views. I met 2Pack and Slowpoke up there and took some 360 shots. Then I got to the Jump Off, which is like walking along the spine of a giant dinosaur. It’s not too steep but the trail is very thin and right along the ridge of the mountains. It was the most memorable section of trail I’ve done so far. I took some great 360 shots there too. Still a few miles to go to the shelter and it’s getting dark!

title: Siler Bald, the best view of NC on the AT!
post:
Just a short hike this evening to the Siler Bald Shelter at mile 114\. Siler Bald is a 5001 foot mountain with no tree cover and awesome views. Unfortunately for me is was super rainy and foggy and I saw nothing at all. But I did meet catch up with Big Man and Refugee at the shelter, and see several older folks going on a shorter section hike that I stayed with a day 2 days before Franklin. It’s nice to see familiar friendly faces when you get to a shelter and get out of the rain.
I also met a couple from Maine who needed a new carabiner to hang their food bag, so I gave them one of mine and we hung our bear bags together. Every night I hang my food at least 8 feet up or put it in a bear box if there is one. This couple started 3 days after me, and they have super nice gear & hiker very fast. They seem serious, but don’t have trail names.

title: Asian King
post: Today is my first ‘Nero day’. It’s a ‘near zero’ day where I only hike a very small number of miles. My friend Meow is doing a Zero Day and staying in Franklin another night. Instead, I’m filling up on Chinese food at the buffet at Asian King and then heading out in the late afternoon and just doing about 5 miles today to the next shelter after Winding Stair Gap, mile 109.8. I was continually eating food for about 3 hours at the buffet and they eventually said I was there too long and needed to finish up, which is fair. I would come back to Franklin, but I have to get moving or I will end up staying here FOREVER.

title: hello world
post:
Here are some words. Today I am starting to work on this blog site. I want to chronicle my adventures by where they happen, not when the happen. Blogs of today are chronological, which has advantages, but I am experimenting with something else. I think this format will be extra good once I start my long hike.

Some features I want to support with this are:

• Markdown editing support
• A 'new post' section
• storing posts in a sqLite db instead of json file
• Automatic Backups
• Custom map colors and styling
• Commenting on each post

title: ETH Denver 2019
post:
I spent the last two weeks in CO, attending ETH Denver as a hacker and mentor. I also spent 6 days in the mountains, skiing out West for the first time and going on adventures. It was a really great experience, and I definitely want to go back in the summer time. CO is a beautiful part of the country.

At Eth Denver I gave a workshop on building ERC-721 tokens on Ethereum.  You can watch it here. (https://youtu.be/49G5eFFu_NE) I think a lot of the learning content in this space is either “Hello World” or really deep dives. The difference between the ends of this spectrum is really vast and many developers I’ve talked to have had a hard time getting past the many beginner tutorials. So the focus of my workshop was on practical integration, and we spent more than half of the time doing live coding and explaining everything as we go. For me, that’s the best way to learn.

After ETH Denver many of the organizers and participants went on a retreat to Breckenridge, CO, for skiing.  I met my Dad in Denver, who flew in from Boston. We drove together to Breckenridge and met up with some ETH Denver folks, but mostly skied just the two of us. It was an awesome place. We also did some day trips to some hot springs and went on a snow shoeing hike too. I bet it’s awesome there in the summer. One of the highlights was playing poker with friends, and my Dad totally hustling everyone. It’s funny to see this older guy come in and smoke a bunch of cockie young crytpo hotshots. It was a great trip.

title: A letter to myself
post:
This is a letter to myself to reflect on where I am now, what is next, why I’m doing it, and give myself a reference for where I was when I return.  Today marks less than a month until I leave for my thru hike attempt of the Appalachian Trail from Georgia to Maine.  I’m planning to leave May 1st, 2019, and to go on a great adventure, which I hope to finish in just under 5 months.

Right now, I am 23 years old, relatively fit, medium length hair, and wearing a red sweatshirt that says Newport which I got for Christmas. I weigh 167 lbs, which is as much as I have ever weighed in my life. I used to exercise more, I used to write more code, I used to spend more time with friends, I used to go outside more. I wish I did those more, but maybe not doing them is a consequence of graduating college and going into ‘real life’. Maybe it’s just how it is. I’ve built a lot of great things in the last year, and had some significant accomplishments in terms of my business and projects, but I’ve also felt myself stagnating and not being as challenged as I used to be. This hike will be a great chance to make friends, to exercise all day, to be outside in the woods. But that’s not necessarily why I am taking 5 months off to do it.

What am I hoping and expecting to find on this hike? I’m not sure exactly. A trip. An adventure. A change. All of those for sure, but that doesn’t fully capture my eagerness to attempt this thru hike. I’m sure I will meet a lot of great people, see a lot of great things, and have some great experiences. But I think most of all I’m looking for a challenge: an experience that is also an accomplishment. I love being in the woods. I’m not afraid of the bears, or people, or logistics. I’m afraid I will miss something when I’m gone, I’m afraid relationships I care about will be strained, I’m afraid I won’t finish by the end of September and it will get too cold. I’ve been thinking about this hike for about three years. It seems now will be the best time in my life to finally take the leap and do it. I have no serious commitments, who knows when that will be true again.

How am I feeling? Great! I’m anxious to get back out into the woods. Sometimes I feel like I live a life of extremes, occasionally programming on my computer for 18 hours at a time, but then going on extended adventures in the woods. I’m having a great time, and excited to get on with my thru hike attempt.

I say thru hike ‘attempt’, but I don’t think I will quit. I know it will not be easy. I’m ready.

title: Approaching the Trail
post:
I flew into Atlanta April 30th. Officially left everyone and everything I’m not taking with me. I’ve never been to Atlanta sio I explored for most of the day and got a shuttle to Amicalola State Park in the evening. The AT starts at Springer Mountain, but there is a 8.8 mile “Approach Trail” from the park to Springer that I will do tomorrow.
Breakfast: 2 packets of dinosaur oatmeal
Snacks: snickers bar, raisins, walnuts, clif bar, fig newtons
Lunch: tortillas and PB&J, pepperoni or summer sausage or tuna packet, gatorade powder
More snacks: dehydrated pineapple slices, little bites muffins
Dinner: quinoa/couscous/rice, dehydrated refried beans/summer sausage/tuna packet, spices, instant mash potatoes, instant mac and cheese

title: Starting Day
post: I’m ready! I got my gear! I got my food! I’m hitting the trail! I slept in a little shelter near the entrance to the park last night and started late, after waiting for the park visitor center to open this morning. I got a ‘hiker tag’ which says I am thru hiker #2329 and I can get it signed at the half-way post in Harpers Ferry and again at the end in Maine. There are about 20 other people starting today with me, but some of them have 70 lbs of gear, and I am not very optimistic on their finishing. Everything seems excited. My pack weighs 32 lbs with all my food and water, there’s a scale at the visitor center. Today is going to be a great day of hiking, with many more to follow.

title: The Quitting Tree
post: Blood Mountain is a great Hike. I’ve been doing about 16+ miles a day so i went right over it. It was foggy at the top, no view, so I didn’t delay and stop there, plus I heard there’s pizza at Neels Gap, at the bottom.  Many people (some that I had been hiking with found the mountain so challenging that by the time they got to the top they had already quit.  As such, at the bottom of the mountain there is a huge oak tree. In the oak there are hundreds of shoes, tied together at the laces. And when hikers quit they throw their shoes up into the tree, as a final I QUIT!  I don’t think I will quit, but I’m seeing several of the folks I started with quitting early. And people going slow, taking a week+ to get to Neels Gap, will quit. I got over it on the morning of my third day. Regardless, it’s a cool tree.

title: Unicoi Gap
post:
Today was my first resupply, a bit earlier than expected. I got a got in the rain and a chance to get a ride into Helen, GA, so I took it. Staying at a Best Western tonight, back to the trail in the morning. My body hurts, still doing at least 15 miles a day. My feet are sore, and it’s hard to stay hydrated. But I’m loving it a lot. I think I’m in a good place and I made the right call to come do this hike.
Animals so far in GA
A hoard of 40 wild boar. A mamma bear and a cub. A big black bear. Bald Eagle. Lots of scary millipedes and centipedes. Mice that live in the shelters and are much more likely to steal your food than bears. Cool ants. Mean ants that stole my raisins. Vultures with long necks. Lots of singing birds. Lots of nice dogs out on hikes.

title: Finished my first week!
post: Made it to Franklin NC in the morning of my 8th day. My feet hurt, I am sore, I’m out of food. The perfect time for a short day of hiking in the morning and taking the rest of the day off in the first big town with a walmart that I’ve reached. I foresee lots of ice cream in my near future. Tonight I stayed at the Gooder Grove Hiker Hostel. It was super relaxed, cheap, I got a bunk. There were a bunch of friendly dogs and I got rides to Ingles for groceries and donuts and ice cream.

title: Albert Mt. Fire Tower
post: Kanye West once said to me ‘keep it a hundred’.Today I hiked 21 miles and passed the 100 mile marker!! My biggest day so far. I was alone for most of the day but making steady progress. I was feeling unmotivated in the afternoon but then I saw Albert Mountain on my map. A huge steep climb, which made me grimace. But then I remembered I had been here before! In 2017 for the solar eclipse I drove down to NC with Abi, Avi, and Jeff. There’s a fire tower on top of Albert Mountain we were going to go up to see the eclipse, but it was too crowded. After I remembered that awesome trip and being on the mountain with my friends, I had a great hike over it. Got some great pictures on the top of the fire tower I will share here as soon as I figure out how to embed 360 images.

title: Muskrat Creep & Fruit Snacks
post: Today was my shortest day so far. I only hiked 12 miles, which is still more than many others are doing. There were dozens on people on the trail. Everyone was friendly, but there were a few hard peaks and I went slow. Feeling worn out tonight, as I stopped early, around 4pm and am journaling in the shelter. I met Munchy, he ate all his food for a week in 2 days after smoking too much weed. I met Moccasins, who has moccasins instead of sandals for camp shoes. And lots of other friendly people that are not thru hiking. At the shelter an old guy who is completing the trail in 50 mile sections over the last 40 years gave me his extra fruit snacks since he was getting off tomorrow, so now I’m happy.  I’ve mostly been hiking with Meow, Big Man, Lola, and Refugee. But Meow and Lola kept going and are way ahead. Big Man and Refugee took a day off in Hiawassee and are way behind so I didn’t see my friends today.
